goal.text: Find out who is moving the land, and keep today's places where they are.

steps.label: Find who is moving the land

plate.narration: You are back on the glacier where it all began. The ice is blue and quiet and enormous. Even the wind has stopped to listen.

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, wondering and a little sad. Short sentences. Nobody dies. The old king is never a monster.

npcVoices.Corvane: He/him, an enormous old faun king, newly awake after a thousand years. Confused above all, courtly, patient and sad. Certain about how things should be, bewildered by how they are. Calls places 'my river', 'my bridge'. Never threatens; never says conquer, punish, servants, destroy or hurt.
npcVoices.Orin Vale: He/him, griffin scholar. Patient, plain speech. Gets the last word only in Rivers Wander.
npcVoices.Seren Wisp: She/her, kitsune teacher. Gentle; holds conditions, never changes where an opening goes.
npcVoices.Bram Lock: He/him, bigfoot guard. Short, practical, warm. Carries a lantern on a pole.
npcVoices.Yeti herder: She/her, the yeti who took the party in on their first night. Patient, dry humor, practical cold-weather care.
npcVoices.Lady Olivia: She/her, unicorn. Humbled and kind; holds, does not push.
npcVoices.Pip Thistledown: He/him, young manticore scout. Eager; notebook and spoon.

arrival.narration: The walking passage winds down into the glacier where all of this began. Snow is falling from a clear sky, and drifting uphill. Your Listening Chime has stopped leaning. Now it points straight down into the ice, and hums. Orin taps the joining lines on his map. "Whoever is moving the land is down there," he says. "Tonight we find out who. And we keep today's places where they are."

variants.text: Lady Olivia walks with you, quieter than usual. Pip trots at her heels.
Lady Olivia walks beside Orin, asking questions and writing down the answers.
Lady Olivia went her own way, to try her own ideas.
Lady Olivia went her own way to try her own ideas, and Pip went with her.
Pip marches beside Bram, taking giant steps.
Far along the ice, the frost wyrm from the readers' hollow keeps pace with you.

herder.narration: A big yeti comes up the ice with a lamp: the herder who took you in on your very first night. Behind her trots the goat kid, the very same one, chewing on Orin's map case. "What you want is under the oldest ice," she says. "The ice stair is quick, and slippery. The crevasse is slower, but I have a rope."

choices.label: Climb down the crevasse on a rope

check_stair.narration: The ice stair spirals down into the glacier, step after glassy step. There is no rail. The chime in your pack hums louder with every turn.
check_stair.prompt: Run down the slippery ice stair without falling

onSuccess.narration: You skip down the last steps and land as light as snow. From the bottom of the stair you can see across the deep ice to a ridge beside a great shimmer. That ridge would hold a brace. You'll remember it.

onFailure.narration: Three steps from the bottom, your feet fly out. You slide the rest of the way on your back, spinning like a plate. Ouch. You saw nothing on the way down but the ceiling.

check_rope.narration: The herder drives a hook into the crevasse wall and ties her rope to it. "Hand over hand," she says. "And don't let the kid chew it." The kid is already chewing it.
check_rope.prompt: Climb down the rope hand over hand, all the way to the bottom

onSuccess.narration: You reach the bottom with sore arms and every finger. Slow, but safe. The kid comes down last, riding on the herder's head.

onFailure.narration: Halfway down, the chewed part gives way. You drop the last bit into soft snow, and the rope lands on your head.

glide.narration: Your griffin spreads wide wings and glides down the crevasse in slow circles. Far across the deep ice you spot a ridge beside a great shimmer, the kind of ridge that would hold a brace. Then you land, and the herder lowers everyone else down on her rope.

kid_bridge.narration: At the bottom, the goat kid bounces past everyone and out onto a thin snow bridge over a crack. Halfway across, the bridge creaks. The kid stops and bleats, the same enormous bleat you heard at the Exchange. "Not again," sighs the herder. "I'll fetch it and take it home. Or you can, and I'll stay with you."

choices.label: Let the herder take it home
Sing the kid back with the low song

check_kid.narration: You creep out onto the snow bridge. It creaks under every step. The kid watches you, chewing, as if this is all a game.
check_kid.prompt: Creep along the creaking snow bridge and carry the kid back

onSuccess.narration: You scoop up the kid and tiptoe back. Behind you, the bridge sighs and drops into the crack. The kid licks your ear. "Good," says the herder, and ties it to her belt with a string.

onFailure.narration: The bridge drops away under your back foot. You leap the last bit with the kid in your arms and land hard on the ice. The kid is fine. You are bruised. The herder ties it to her belt with a string, very firmly.

sing_kid.narration: Your songkeeper sings the low song, the yetis' own. The kid's ears swivel, and it trots straight back across the bridge just before the bridge falls in. The herder hums along, pleased, and ties the kid to her belt with a string.

herder_goes.narration: The herder steps out onto the bridge, light as a cloud for someone so big, and tucks the kid under her arm. "I'll take this one home," she says. "Then I'll come back with blankets. Go on. Follow your chime." Her lamp bobs away, back up the crevasse.

rest.narration: Behind a rib of old ice, out of the wind, Bram hangs his lantern and Orin opens the last of the supper bag. Everyone eats with their mittens on. Through a crack in the ice rib, you can see a shimmer, far off, moving slowly, like breath. There is time to do one thing before you go on.

variants.text: The herder pours hot broth from a pot she has carried the whole way. The kid tries to drink it.

choices.label: Climb the ice rib and study the ridge

warm_up.narration: You squash together in a heap, with Seren's tail over everyone's knees like a blanket. Bram is the warmest. Bram is always the warmest. By the time you get up, your fingers work again.

choices.label: Go on into the old ice

ridge_look.narration: You climb the ice rib with Seren and peer over the top. Far across the deep ice, a ridge stands beside a great shimmer. "See that ridge?" Seren whispers. "Brace it, and anything open beside it closes faster." Your fingers are freezing, but now you know where to go.

choices.label: Go on into the old ice

broth.narration: The herder's broth tastes of smoke and onions, and it warms you right down to your toes. She looks back the way you came. "Warm feet climb better," she says, and pours you seconds.

choices.label: Go on into the old ice

old_ice.narration: The passage opens into a chamber of old ice, so old it is nearly black. It is quiet as a held breath. The snow that slid down from the ledge drifts across the floor, all of it going the same way. Seren puts a finger to her lips. "This ice is very old," she whispers. "Walk softly."

variants.text: You remember the reading room, and the old yeti's warning. Do not shout near the old ice. You don't know what you might wake.

check_quiet.narration: Every step on the old ice could crack like a dropped plate. Far ahead, past a ridge, something shimmers, huge and slow. Someone down there is talking to himself.
check_quiet.prompt: Cross the old ice without a single crunch

onSuccess.narration: Not one crunch. Whoever is talking up ahead has no idea you are coming.

onFailure.narration: CRACK. The ice booms like a drum, and icicles rain down around you. One bonks you on the head. Up ahead, the talking stops.

frozen.narration: On the way to the ridge, things are frozen into the old ice, caught in the middle of sliding: a fence post, a wheelbarrow, a little rowboat with its oars still in. Every one of them leans the same way, toward the shimmer. Bram taps a painted board stuck in the ice. It says FRESH NOODLES. "That's from the Exchange," he says. "From the quay."

figure.narration: You peek over the ridge. Below, a great tear hangs in the air, wider than a house. Through it, faraway ground slides past: a valley, a river, a hill, all moving. Under it, a tall figure bends over an old map on the ice. "Why is the river on the wrong side of the mountain?" he asks the map. "It was never on that side." In your pack, the chime rings all by itself.

variants.text: He has not seen you yet. He sounds puzzled, not angry. Lost, almost.
He turns toward the sound, slowly, the way a grandfather turns when someone drops a spoon.

reveal.narration: He straightens up, and up. He is an enormous faun with a long mustache tied back with a faded ribbon. He bows, slow and courtly. "I am Corvane. I was king here, when the land lay in its proper places. My kingdom was called Pangea: all the lands, joined in one. Do you know how long I have waited to see my rivers run the right way again?" So here is the truth. Corvane is the one moving the land. He slept in this ice for a thousand years, until the mountain woke and let him go. Now he is putting every place back where it was in his day.

his_story.narration: Corvane smooths his old map with one huge, careful hand. Orin looks from it to his own joining lines, and his beak drops open. They are the same shape. "I have been setting things right," Corvane says. "My bridge. My river. My island in the sky. One by one, home again. You have walked my land. You know how it should be. Will you help me finish?"

choices.label: Ask him why it matters so much
Tell him no, it has to stop

why_home.narration: Corvane is quiet for a long moment. "Because everything I loved is in the old places," he says. "My river is where I learned to swim. My bridge is where my people waved me home. I went to sleep, and when I woke, it was all moved, and nobody asked me." He looks at you, surprised. "You are the first to ask me anything."

told_no.narration: Corvane blinks down at you, as if a pebble had spoken. "Stop?" he says. "But it is nearly right." Bram steps up beside you, big and steady, and plants his feet. "They said no," Bram rumbles. "I'm with them." Corvane looks at Bram's big feet, then back at his map, puzzled.

his_map.narration: Corvane lifts his hands, and the great tear widens. Through it, a whole valley tips, ready to slide, homes and all. "Please stand aside," he says kindly. "I am nearly home." Orin's feathers stand on end. There is no time to talk it over. What will you do?

choices.label: Show him today's map, and the homes on it
Ask him what home looked like
Let Olivia tell him what happened to her

check_force.narration: You grab one edge of the tear, and Bram grabs the other. It feels like holding a curtain in a gale. Corvane gasps. "No, no, you will tear it!"
check_force.prompt: Haul the tear's edges together and pin them against the ice

onSuccess.narration: You haul, and the edges come together with a snap like a sail. Bram jams an ice rib across the gap to hold it. The tear is narrower now, and pinned.

onFailure.narration: The edge rips out of your grip and flings you across the ice. Bram catches you, just. The tear flaps wide again.

check_force_bram.narration: Bram is already moving. "You take the top, I take the bottom," he says, and grabs the tear's edge like a tent flap in a storm.
check_force_bram.prompt: Haul the top of the tear down to Bram's edge

onSuccess.narration: Top meets bottom with a snap like a sail. Bram jams an ice rib across the gap. "Pinned," he grunts.

onFailure.narration: The top edge whips out of your hands and knocks you flat. Bram lets go to help you up, and the tear flaps wide again.

check_show.narration: You hold up Orin's map, today's map, with all its towns and roads and little houses. "Look," you say. "People live there now." Corvane bends down, very low, to see.
check_show.prompt: Help Corvane really see the homes on today's map

onSuccess.narration: He looks for a long time. He touches one little house with the tip of his finger. "My old map left those out," he murmurs. His hands lower, just a little.

onFailure.narration: "Those are not on my map," he says, puzzled, and turns back to his tear. While you talked, a far valley slid one hill farther from home.

asked_home.narration: "What did home look like?" you ask. Corvane's hands stop. "Reeds," he says. "A wooden bridge. My mother's boat." Then he looks through the tear at a village sliding past, with its washing still on the line. "Someone else's mother," he says slowly. His hands lower, just a little.

olivia_tells.narration: Olivia steps up, quite pale. "I called an opening once," she tells him. "Only to ask. It didn't do one thing I wanted. The colors were wrong, and it pulled at everything." Corvane stares at her. "Yes," he says slowly. "They do that now." His hands lower, just a little.

wrong_colors.narration: Corvane raises his hands to pull harder. The tear flares, and colors pour out of it, colors nobody chose, sliding like oil on a puddle. Corvane stares. "That is not the color I asked for," he says, and suddenly he looks very old. "He can open them, but he can't tell them what to do," Seren whispers. "Nobody can. Now, while he's surprised. Your pieces. Show the land where it belongs today."

variants.text: "That's exactly what happened to me," Olivia whispers.
"That's exactly what happened to me," Olivia whispers.
Somewhere along the tear, an edge is pinned, and it creaks.

choices.label: Put your hand on the old ice

anchor_one.narration: Put your hand flat on the old ice and think of the river the memory ice showed you. Then think of it as it runs today, down its own valley, past the homes along its banks. Think of it hard, just as it is now.

variants.text: Put your hand flat on the old ice and think of the buried bridge, standing on the mudflats where it is now, with the tide creeping in around its gray arches. Think of it hard, just as it is now.

anchor_one.prompt: Hold your piece of today's land in your mind, and press it into the ice

onSuccess.narration: Under your hand, the ice goes warm, then still. In the tear, a whole piece of land stops sliding and settles where it belongs today.

onFailure.narration: The pull drags at your arm, and you nearly let go. Then the ice goes still under your hand. The land in the tear settles, but a field's width from where it was this morning.

corvane_one.narration: Corvane spins around, his cloak swirling. "Those stones are mine," he says. "I set them there." He pulls, hard. The land in the tear does not move for him. It stays where today put it. He frowns at his hands, as if they had forgotten how.

anchor_two.narration: Now the next piece. Think of the buried bridge, standing on the mudflats where it is now, with the tide creeping in around its gray arches, specked white like salt on bread. Think of it hard, just as it is now.

variants.text: Now the next piece. Think of the island that came back, and of the land below it as it is today, not as the old carving showed. Think of the island floating where it floats now. Think of it hard.
Now the next piece. Think of the island that came back, and of the land below it as it is today, not as the old carving showed. Think of the island floating where it floats now. Think of it hard.
Somewhere far above, the island lurches. The temple keepers have not finished mending its landing.

anchor_two.prompt: Hold your next piece of today's land in your mind, and press it into the ice

onSuccess.narration: The ice goes warm again, then still. In the tear, a second piece of land settles where it belongs today. The great tear shudders and breaks apart.

onFailure.narration: Your hand slides on the ice, and the pull drags you a step closer to the tear before you hold. A second piece of land settles, a little crooked. The great tear shudders and breaks apart.

corvane_two.narration: Corvane stares at you, and at the land in the tear, holding still. "It listens to you?" he says. He sounds amazed, not angry. Then he grabs the last seam of his broken tear with both hands and holds it open. "Two places hold," says Seren. "Orin and I can wait on a rescue lane, in case anything goes wrong. Or we can stand at the ridge with you. Is there anything else?"

variants.text: You have one more piece. You carried all three.
Out on the ice, the frost wyrm lifts its long head, as if it heard its name.
Olivia steps up beside you. "A condition," she says, "not a command. I can help hold."

choices.label: Keep Orin and Seren back on the rescue lane
Bring Orin and Seren to the ridge with you
Hold your third piece, the island
Call the frost wyrm to help

anchor_three.narration: Your last piece. Think of the island that came back, and of the land below it as it is today, not as the old carving showed. Think of the island floating where it floats now. Think of it hard.

variants.text: Somewhere far above, the island lurches. The temple keepers have not finished mending its landing.

anchor_three.prompt: Hold the island as it is today, and press it into the ice

onSuccess.narration: A third time, the ice goes warm and still. High above, the island stops drifting and stays where it floats today.

onFailure.narration: The pull yanks at you, and you scrape along the ice before you hold. High above, the island settles, a little off from where it was.

wyrm_anchor.narration: You call to the frost wyrm, low and slow, the way the readers taught you. You cannot make it do anything. You can only ask.
wyrm_anchor.prompt: Ask the frost wyrm to curl around the land as it is

onSuccess.narration: The wyrm slides across the ice and curls its long, cold body around the ridge, like a cat around a teacup. The land under it goes still.

onFailure.narration: The wyrm takes its time, sniffs the tear and sneezes frost on you. Then it curls around the ridge anyway, like a cat around a teacup. The land under it goes still.

olivia_anchor.narration: Olivia puts her hoof on the ice beside your hand. "Tell me what to hold," she says. "I won't push. I promise."
olivia_anchor.prompt: Hold the land as it is, with Olivia, without pushing

onSuccess.narration: You hold it together, and she does not push once. The land goes still under both of you. Olivia laughs out loud, surprised. "It listened!"

onFailure.narration: Olivia pushes, just a little, from habit. The ice bucks, and you both sit down hard. Then she breathes out, and holds instead. The land goes still.

seam.narration: Only one seam is left of the great tear, glowing beside the ridge. Corvane holds it open with both hands. Two bone crawlers tumble out of it, pulled from somewhere very far away, and blink in the cold. "Please," Corvane says. "I only want to go home."

variants.text: Orin and Seren wait back on the rescue lane, ready if anything goes wrong.
You know where the ridge will hold a brace.

choices.label: Brace the ridge and close the seam fast

seam_weak.narration: Three places hold. Only one thin seam is left of the great tear, flickering beside the ridge. Corvane holds it open with both hands, but his arms are shaking. One bone crawler tumbles out, pulled from somewhere very far away, and blinks in the cold. "Please," Corvane says. "I only want to go home."

variants.text: The frost wyrm stays curled around the ridge, humming like a kettle.
Olivia keeps her hoof on the ice, holding, not pushing.
You know where the ridge will hold a brace.

choices.label: Brace the ridge and close the seam fast

fight_standard.narration: Corvane holds the last seam open. "I only want to go home," he says. Beside him, two bone crawlers scuttle out of its light. Drive them off, or hold the ridge for four turns to close the seam. The seam's pull bites anyone who stops on it.

objectives.label: Hold the ridge and close the last seam

fight_standard_braced.narration: Corvane holds the last seam open. "I only want to go home," he says. Beside him, two bone crawlers scuttle out of its light. Drive them off, or hold the ridge for three turns to close the seam. The seam's pull bites anyone who stops on it.

objectives.label: Hold the ridge and close the last seam

fight_weakened.narration: Corvane holds the last seam open. "I only want to go home," he says. Beside him, one bone crawler scuttles out of its light. Drive them off, or hold the ridge for four turns to close the seam. The seam's pull bites anyone who stops on it.

objectives.label: Hold the ridge and close the last seam

fight_weakened_braced.narration: Corvane holds the last seam open. "I only want to go home," he says. Beside him, one bone crawler scuttles out of its light. Drive them off, or hold the ridge for three turns to close the seam. The seam's pull bites anyone who stops on it.

objectives.label: Hold the ridge and close the last seam

spent.narration: The last seam folds shut with a soft pop, like a bubble. Corvane's hands drop. The crawlers turn around and scuttle off into the ice, looking for the way home. The glacier goes so quiet you can hear the ribbon fall onto his old map. Corvane sits down on the ice, very slowly. "It was a very good map," he says.

variants.text: You held the ridge until the seam closed. Nobody had to knock him down.
You did it on the second try, and some places slid a little before you did.

blanket.narration: The herder hurries over the ice with her lamp and an armful of blankets, the goat kid trotting behind her on its string. She shakes out the biggest blanket you have ever seen. It is just big enough for Corvane. He looks like someone who has been cold for a very long time.

help_him.narration: Corvane looks at the blanket, and then at all of you, as if he does not know what to do. The goat kid starts chewing the corner of his old map. "Ask before you wrap him," the herder whispers. What will you do?

choices.label: Lay his map beside today's map

wrap.narration: You hold out the blanket, and wait. After a long moment, Corvane bows his head and lets you put it around his shoulders. He pulls it tight. "Thank you," he says. "It has been a very long time since anyone asked me anything."

maps_side.narration: You rescue his old map from the goat and lay it on the ice. Then you put Orin's map right beside it, joining lines and little houses and all. Corvane looks from one to the other. For the first time, he looks longest at the new one. "So many roofs," he says softly. "I did not put those there."

chime_straight.narration: In your pack, the Listening Chime gives one last soft ring, and stops. You take it out. For the first time since the travelers gave it to you, it hangs straight down. It does not lean anywhere at all. The snow drifting across the floor settles, and stays. "Moved things go home," Orin says quietly. "And so must he. But which home?"

fate.narration: The herder sets down her lamp. "The ice can keep him," she says, "asleep, with his memories safe. Or he can live with us, and learn the names of things as they are now." Corvane looks at the deep ice, and then at the plain walking door the yetis cut in the wall long ago. "You found my places," he says to you. "You choose."

keepers_epilogue.narration: The yetis make a quiet place deep in the ice. Corvane folds his old map and lies down beneath his blanket, with the map on his chest. "Wake me if the rivers ever forget their way," he says, and closes his eyes. The ice keeps him, and he keeps the memory. The land stays where it is, today's land, with all its roofs, and the Riftseekers write it all down. In the records of the glacier, your party is called the Glacier Keepers.

variants.text: Before he slept, he asked for a copy of today's map, to keep beside his own.
He kept the blanket.
A few places settled a little crooked tonight, a field here, a hill there. The Riftseekers will draw them in.
Some places slid before the seam closed. Today's map has a scar on it now, and the Riftseekers will mend what they can.
Lady Olivia stays to study with Orin, testing one thing at a time.
Lady Olivia helps the watchers hold the last loose ground, humbled and glad.
Somewhere far off, Lady Olivia is trying her own way. Nobody is cross with her for it.
Pip writes the whole story down for Bram, with drawings.
Wherever Olivia is, Pip is writing it all down.
The frost wyrm curls up outside the readers' hollow again, a good neighbor.
High in the sky, the island that came back drifts gently where the temple keepers settled it.
Up in the sky, the temple keepers mend their landing, plank by plank.

listened_epilogue.narration: Corvane goes with the herder through the plain walking door, to the yetis' broad table. They spread the present map in front of him, with all its roofs and roads. He points to a valley. "Then tell me what you call this valley now." The herder, who keeps watch on the old ice, tells him. He writes it down, very carefully. The land stays where it is. In the records of the glacier, your party is called the Ones Who Listened.

variants.text: He keeps his old map too, folded small, under the new one.
He wears the blanket like a cloak.
A few places settled a little crooked tonight, a field here, a hill there. The Riftseekers will draw them in.
Some places slid before the seam closed. Today's map has a scar on it now, and the Riftseekers will mend what they can.
Lady Olivia stays to study with Orin, testing one thing at a time.
Lady Olivia helps the watchers hold the last loose ground, humbled and glad.
Somewhere far off, Lady Olivia is trying her own way. Nobody is cross with her for it.
Pip writes the whole story down for Bram, with drawings.
Wherever Olivia is, Pip is writing it all down.
The frost wyrm curls up outside the readers' hollow again, a good neighbor.
High in the sky, the island that came back drifts gently where the temple keepers settled it.
Up in the sky, the temple keepers mend their landing, plank by plank.

loss_recover.narration: The seam's pull knocks everyone flat and drags you across the ice. Bram scoops up whoever he can reach, and you all scramble back behind the ridge. In the seam, some places slide a little farther from home. Corvane still holds it open. But the pull comes in breaths, and when it breathes out, there will be one more chance.

loss_plan.narration: Seren counts the breaths of the pull. In, out. In, out. "On the next one," she says. "Or never." How will you get back to the ridge?

choices.label: Rush the ridge when the pull breathes out
Let Orin and Seren hold the ridge with you
Let Pip run Bram's rope to the ridge
Steer by the island the keepers settled

recover_check.narration: The pull breathes in. Breathes out. Now! You run for the ridge across the bucking ice.
recover_check.prompt: Rush the ridge on the breath out and brace it before the pull comes back

onSuccess.narration: You reach the ridge and brace it with everything you have. The seam shudders.

onFailure.narration: Your feet go out from under you on the breath in, and the pull drags you back behind the ridge.

recover_ask.narration: You walk right up to Corvane, slowly, with your hands open. He remembers you. He remembers the homes.
recover_ask.prompt: Ask Corvane, kindly, to let the seam go

onSuccess.narration: "Let it go," you say. "Please." Corvane looks at his hands for a long moment. Then he opens them.

onFailure.narration: He wants to. You can see he wants to. But his hands will not open, and the pull drags you back behind the ridge.

recover_reserve.narration: Orin and Seren have been waiting on the rescue lane for exactly this. "Together," says Orin. You run for the ridge, all of you at once.
recover_reserve.prompt: Brace the ridge together with Orin and Seren

onSuccess.narration: Three pairs of hands are better than one. The ridge holds.

onFailure.narration: Your feet go out from under you on the breath in, and the pull drags you back behind the ridge.

recover_pip.narration: Pip grabs the end of Bram's rope in his teeth and scampers for the ridge on the breath out, small and fast, under the pull. "Real scouts go first," he says, "when it's their turn!"
recover_pip.prompt: Follow Pip's rope to the ridge and brace it

onSuccess.narration: Pip ties the rope off at the ridge, and you haul yourselves along it, and brace the ridge.

onFailure.narration: Your feet go out from under you on the breath in, and the pull drags you back behind the ridge.

recover_island.narration: Through the broken tear, high above, you can see the island that came back, sitting still where the temple keepers settled it. Keep it in sight, like a star, and walk straight.
recover_island.prompt: Keep the settled island in sight and walk straight to the ridge

onSuccess.narration: The island never moves, so neither do you. You reach the ridge and brace it.

onFailure.narration: Your feet go out from under you on the breath in, and the pull drags you back behind the ridge.

loss_second_failed.narration: Then, all at once, the pull stops. Corvane's strength is spent, and the seam folds shut on its own. But in its last flicker you see rivers in new beds and a valley turned around. They stay that way. Corvane sits down on the ice, holding a map that does not fit anything anymore. "It was a very good map," he says.

loss_epilogue.narration: The herder wraps Corvane in her biggest blanket and leads him up toward the yetis' door. Some rivers have wandered. Some valleys have swapped places. Nothing is broken that cannot be mended, but everything needs drawing again, and the Riftseekers will draw it. Orin smooths out a fresh page and folds the old joining lines under it. "Then we learn the new map," he says. In the records of the glacier, this story is called Rivers Wander.
